Title: Seeded foreign-row invisibility proof for every CDR-088 tenant-data read
Security and tenant considerations: Tenant isolation is the whole subject. The three CDR-088 matrix blocks serving tenant data (roadmap read, artifact reads, approvals inbox) each proved only refusal AT COMPANY SCOPE and disclosed that they could not prove an EXISTING foreign row stays invisible. Two of the three disclosures were factually wrong: both cited an FK to a 'runs' table that does not exist in this schema, when the real constraint is a tenant-pinned composite onto task_runs, which the CDR-089 block in the same file already seeds. Those two matrices were withheld on an unverified premise rather than a real constraint.
Acceptance criteria: The CDR-088 disclosure list is ZERO, not smaller by one. Each of the three blocks seeds a real foreign row in a nested beforeEach, asserts its existence on the OWNER connection FIRST (pinned to the specific id), then proves byte-identical refusal WITH the row present; each also seeds the caller's own company as a positive control so the negative is not satisfiable by a read that returns nothing to anybody. The two incorrect comments are corrected in place, each naming the real constraint and its migration line.
Test evidence: Local real-PostgreSQL run of the adversarial suite: 54 passed / 54, zero skipped; full gate 284 files / 4207 tests, zero skips. MUTATION-PROVEN, with the FIRST mutation report retracted as wrong: it claimed 10 red tests across three blocks, but 8 of those were beforeEach fixture errors (two version-1 rows in one company violating understanding_documents_company_version_uq and policies_company_version_uq), not assertions - the count was reported without reading why each test was red. The corrected evidence is two collision-free mutations producing 5 assertion failures, each quoted in CDR-093 s3.2: marker-collision fires the roadmap, approvals and task-board invisibility assertions; artifact relocation fires 'B's artifact must not surface inside A' and the artifact-granularity byte-identity check. Restored byte-for-byte after each run and re-verified green. Hosted exact-head CI at zero skips is the merge gate and the only real-database evidence.
Explicit exclusions: No production code changes - tests, fixtures and three corrected comments only. The CDR-089 run block is untouched because it already seeds and already proves its own case. The fixtures are DATABASE-LEVEL and deliberately do not pass through use-case contract validation, so they prove nothing about whether the write paths are correct; isolation is the only claim made. ACBP-API-001 through 009 are a concurrent session's tickets, are recorded in AUTONOMOUS-RUN-LOG.md, and are deliberately NOT backfilled here.

Title: Restore true startup visibility for model-provider misconfiguration
Surfaces touched: apps/web/src/server/webhooks/clerk-runtime.ts; a new apps/web/src/instrumentation.ts (does not exist today)
Security and tenant considerations: None. This changes WHEN an existing local failure is surfaced, not who may see anything: no tenant data, no authorization decision, no new surface. The one thing to keep true is that the log line stays FACT-ONLY - model_provider.not_configured today carries a consequence and an unaffected-scope note and never the parser message, because a config error message can quote the offending value. Any instrumentation hook must preserve that, and must stay NON-FATAL for the same reason the current catch is: this runtime serves every route, so a fatal model misconfiguration would take down the 32 routes that never touch a model along with the 4 that do.
Acceptance criteria: Starting the web app with an absent or unparseable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY emits model_provider.not_configured BEFORE any request is served, and a TEST proves it - not a comment asserting it. The acceptance bar is specifically that the proof is executable, because this row exists precisely because two comments claimed the property in prose while the code did not deliver it.
Test evidence: MET, and the framework half is proven empirically rather than cited. apps/web/src/instrumentation.ts exports register(), which Next 16 runs once per server process before the first request. instrumentation.test.ts DRIVES register() rather than asserting anything about it - absent key emits model_provider.not_configured; a valid configuration emits nothing (CONTROL); non-fatal; register.length is 0 so Next can call it with no arguments; importing the module has no side effect. The acceptance bar was written as "a test proves it, not a comment asserting it", because this row exists precisely because prose claimed a property the code did not have. THE FRAMEWORK CONTRACT IS SEPARATELY PROVEN: next build --webpack emits .next/server/instrumentation.js containing model_provider.not_configured - the exact path Next loads at boot - so the source file really is resolved at apps/web/src/instrumentation.ts. The unit suite states the boundary it cannot cross: it proves this repository half of the property, not that Next schedules register(). ONE definition serves both paths (apps/web/src/server/startup/model-provider-report.ts, 6 tests): FACT-ONLY (payload keys are exactly consequence and unaffected, and a planted offending value never reaches the logger) and NON-FATAL. clerk-runtime.ts now delegates to it, so the boot line and the composition line cannot drift. Three surfaces that asserted the old behaviour were corrected in the same change: packages/config/src/index.ts, CDR-094 (resolution note; the ruling itself left intact) and this row.
Explicit exclusions: DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT under ACBP-API-011 (owner ruling 2026-08-19): the two false comments were corrected to describe first-request firing, and whether an instrumentation hook should restore boot-time visibility is filed here rather than decided inside a routing ticket. No scaffolding toward it exists. Also excluded: any change to the parser itself - parseModelProviderConfig already throws unconditionally, and the missing property belongs to the composition path, not to it.
